text:
All verified:

- **Issue case**: `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)` now returns `["aaa bbb"]` (exactly 7 chars, stays on one line)
- **Overlong words** still split correctly: `wrap("hello world", 5)` → `["hello", "world"]`, and a 20-char word at width 5 → four 5-char lines
- **Full test suite passes**

The fix was a one-character change in `wrapper/wrap.py`: the greedy join condition used `< width` instead of `<= width`, so any word that would have filled the line exactly was pushed to the next line, making every line one character short.

arguments.summary: Fixed the off-by-one in wrapper/wrap.py: the greedy join condition `len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width` was changed to `<= width`, so a word that would fill the line exactly (e.g. `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)`) now stays on the same line instead of being pushed to the next. Overlong-word splitting is uncha...
